title: Stretches Over Which Qualifying Settled Trips Are Counted
content:
Which stretch the qualifying settled trips of a Keyturn Host Payout Account are counted over turns on how long the payout account has been open, because a shorter record is annualised rather than read as a whole year's trading. The age of the account is counted in whole calendar days from the day the account was opened up to that day.

| Age of the payout account | Trips counted |
|---|---|
| 365 calendar days or longer | The trip earnings credited in the twelve months up to that day are counted |
| 92 calendar days or longer but less than 365 | The trip earnings credited in the three months up to that day are counted and multiplied by four |
| Under 92 calendar days | Only the trip earnings credited in the month up to that day are counted |

Trip earnings are counted one to an entry.

## Both sides of each boundary

At 365 calendar days the first row governs; at 364 the second does. At 92 calendar days the second row governs; at 91 the third does.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account credited with 30 trip earnings in the twelve months up to that day, 9 in the three months up to that day and 4 in the month up to that day. The qualifying settled trips are 30 where the account has been open 400 calendar days, 36 where it has been open 200 calendar days, and 4 where it has been open 60 calendar days.
